summary: Clipping tab: finds objects sunk into each other and paints the buried part, without judging whether it was intended.
overview: Answers one question: is this particular thing placed wrong. A crate half inside the floor, a post buried in a wall, a barrel intersecting the stairs — all of it invisible while you are zoomed in placing the next prop, and all of it obvious to a player.

It is built around a limitation it refuses to hide: nothing can tell whether an intersection was intended. A post sunk into a wall may be exactly right. So it finds candidates cheaply, paints what is actually buried, and leaves the call to you — it never reports an error and never fixes anything.

walkthrough.step: Set Subject Mask to the things you are checking, and Target Mask to what they might be buried in.
walkthrough.whatYouSee: Only SUBJECTS get painted. That asymmetry is the point: you want the crate reddened where it is buried, not the floor it is buried in, so floors and architecture never light up.

walkthrough.step: Choose Collider or Mesh for the display mode.
walkthrough.whatYouSee: Collider checks the shapes that actually block the player — right for a traversal or metrics pass. Mesh checks the visual model — right for a visual-quality pass. They disagree often, and which one is correct depends entirely on what you are checking for.

walkthrough.step: Press Scan Whole Level, or Scan Selection for just what you have highlighted.
walkthrough.whatYouSee: A result list with a Select button per row, and the flagged objects tinted in the Scene view.

walkthrough.step: Leave Highlight Style on Buried Portion Only.
walkthrough.whatYouSee: Only the part of the object that is inside other geometry gets painted, via a ZTest Greater shader pass. You see how DEEP something is sunk, not merely that it is. Whole Object tints the entire thing instead, which is easier to spot from a distance but tells you less.

walkthrough.step: Raise Overlap Tolerance if ordinary resting contact keeps appearing.
walkthrough.whatYouSee: Fewer results. An object must interpenetrate by more than the tolerance to be flagged, which is what keeps a crate merely sitting on a floor out of the list.

walkthrough.step: Press Clear All Highlights when you are done.
walkthrough.whatYouSee: The Scene view returns to normal. Switching away from the tab also stops its drawing.

useCases: A pre-art pass over a greybox level, catching props pushed through the floor by a careless drag.
Checking a kitbashed set piece where many meshes were deliberately overlapped, to find the ones that overlap by more than you meant.
Verifying that collision, rather than just the visual mesh, is clean along a route the player walks.

gotchas.title: Candidates, not errors
gotchas.body: An empty result list means 'nothing obvious at this tolerance and these masks', not 'the level is correct'. And a full list is not a list of bugs — deliberate intersections are extremely common in level art.

gotchas.title: Collider mode and Mesh mode will disagree
gotchas.body: A prop whose collider is a simple box can read as clean in Collider mode while its visual mesh is clearly poking through a wall, and vice versa. Pick the mode that matches the question you are asking rather than treating either as the truth.
